metadata.title: MARKETS LIVE: Wall Street pares losses as Dow stages late-session recovery

content.text:
4:20pm: A late recovery
US stocks staged a sharp recovery on Wednesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average clawing back from an early plunge of more than 1,100 points to finish higher, while technology shares remained under pressure.
The Dow closed up 164 points, or 0.3%, at 50,183. The S&P 500 fell 18 points, or 0.3%, to 7,183, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 148 points, or 0.6%, to 23,586.
The late-session turnaround helped limit what had been shaping up as another difficult day for Wall Street, although the split between the blue-chip Dow and its technology-heavy counterparts reflected continued investor caution around AI-related spending and semiconductor valuations.
Defensive stocks helped support the Dow's recovery, while chipmakers including Nvidia and Micron remained under pressure as investors reassessed the scale and financing of AI infrastructure investment.
The technology sell-off was compounded by the announcement of new US tariffs of 20% on 14 trading partners, adding another source of uncertainty for companies exposed to global supply chains.
Investors also had fresh inflation data to digest, with the personal consumption expenditures price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, rising to 3.8% year over year in October.
The reading reinforced concerns that inflation remains stubbornly high and could complicate the Fed's plans for monetary policy. It also fuelled speculation that policymakers may consider a more aggressive approach at their December meeting, including the possibility of a 50-basis-point rate increase.
Markets will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving, leaving investors to reflect on a volatile session and a technology-led correction that has continued to test confidence in the AI trade.
3:45pm: Small cap wrap
VivoPower PLC (NASDAQ:VIVO) is seeing growing demand for 40MW to 50MW Nordic data center sites, including from major operators previously focused on projects above 100MW.
NextSource Materials Inc. (TSX:NEXT, OTCQB:NSRCF) has signed a binding agreement with Hanwa and JOGMEC covering the development, funding and operation of its planned UAE battery anode facility.
374Water Inc (NASDAQ:SCWO) said its upgraded AirSCWO 6 system processed 59% more biosolids per day in its latest factory test than in the original test.
Bit Digital Inc (NASDAQ:BTBT) has repaid $50 million of debt to Galaxy Digital (TSX-V:GLXY), halving its outstanding borrowings to $50 million through the sale of 29,825 ETH.
Graphene Manufacturing Group Ltd (TSX-V:GMG, OTCQX:GMGMF) reported progress in improving production quality at its Gen 2.0 graphene plant, which is designed to produce 10 tonnes annually.
1911 Gold Corp (TSX-V:AUMB, OTCQB:AUMBF) has launched a financing targeting up to C$12 million to fund exploration and development at its True North project in Manitoba.
Sintana Energy Inc (TSX-V:SEI, OTCQB:SEUSF, AIM:SEI) has completed a US$2.5 million investment for an indirect 5% stake in Angola's KON-16 block, where drilling is targeted for 2027.
2:40pm: Market movers
HP Inc (NYSE:HPQ) shares rose nearly 11% after the company beat fourth-quarter earnings and revenue expectations, despite a cautious fiscal 2027 outlook.
Ambarella Inc. (NASDAQ:AMBA) fell 20% after missing earnings expectations and warning that memory shortages were disrupting customer orders.
Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD) fell nearly 9% as concerns over AI valuations, US tariffs and interest rates triggered a broad chip stock sell-off.
Nutanix Inc (NASDAQ:NTNX) dropped 19% despite beating quarterly revenue expectations, as investors reacted to an unchanged sales outlook and CEO succession plans.
Urban Outfitters, Inc. (NASDAQ:URBN) fell 12% after comparable sales growth slowed to 4.4%, despite record quarterly revenue of $1.67 billion.
Autodesk Inc (NASDAQ:ADSK) reported a 16.6% increase in fiscal third-quarter revenue to $2.16 billion, beating analyst expectations for sales and earnings.
1:30pm: Chip stocks tumble
Global chip stocks tumbled on Wednesday, with Nvidia and memory makers leading a broad retreat in technology shares as concerns over artificial intelligence valuations, US tariffs and interest rates weighed on investor sentiment.
Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD) (Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD), Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD)) fell nearly 9%, reversing much of Monday's rally following comments and developments involving CEO Jensen Huang.
Chip designer Arm Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:ARM) (Arm Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:ARM)) dropped 8%, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (ADR) (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (ADR) (NYSE:TSM)), which manufactures Nvidia's chips, and semiconductor equipment maker ASML Holding NV (NASDAQ:ASML, XETRA:ASME) (ASML Holding NV (NASDAQ:ASML, XETRA:ASME), ASML Holding NV (NASDAQ:ASML, XETRA:ASME)) each lost more than 3%.
Memory chipmakers Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU) (Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU)) and South Korea's SK Hynix fell roughly 10%, giving back some of Monday's double-digit gains. Storage companies Sandisk, Seagate Technology and Western Digital also declined.
"Investors are back to dumping tech stocks with indecent haste, but now everything else is being dragged into it too," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG.
He said Monday's rally, which followed Huang's return to the spotlight, had provided markets with only a brief reprieve, adding that US investors were focused on getting through the Thanksgiving holiday without further losses.
12:10pm: FTSE rally fades
The FTSE started Wednesday on the front foot but couldn't manage to hold its gains throughout the day, finishing 0.4% lower at 10,427 points.
"There's a definite flight to safety feel on the FTSE 100, with the leaderboard dominated by dividend stocks with reliable revenue streams," said IG's Chris Beauchamp.
"The selling at the other end has been widespread, and gold's slump below $3500 means that miners are out of favour once again.
"Losses are contained compared to the US, but that is unlikely to last."
11:00am: Growth accelerates
US economic growth accelerated more than expected in the third quarter, while inflation remained elevated, adding to uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's next interest rate decision.
Second-estimate data showed US GDP grew at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, up from the previous estimate of 3.4% and ahead of the 3.5% consensus forecast.
However, the inflation picture offered less encouragement. Core personal consumption expenditures (PCE), the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, rose 3.3% year over year in October, above the 3.2% estimate and up from 3.1% previously. Headline PCE inflation increased to 3.8% from 3.7%, in line with expectations.
Both core and headline PCE rose 0.3% month over month, matching forecasts. Consumer spending increased 0.3%, below the 0.4% expected.
Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer at Northlight Asset Management, said the GDP figure showed the economy was booming, but persistent inflation was unlikely to persuade the Fed to remain on hold.
He suggested the newly announced tariffs could add pressure to financial markets and potentially give policymakers room to delay tightening, but said a 25-basis-point rate increase in December remained likely.
"Between the AI angst and the newly announced tariffs, it doesn't look like the Santa Claus rally is in store for us this year," Zaccarelli added.
9:45 am ET: Major United States stock indexes fell sharply at the opening bell
United States stock markets opened significantly lower as a sharp sell-off in technology shares wiped billions of dollars off company valuations.
The Nasdaq Composite index tumbled 3% within minutes of the opening bell as anxiety over artificial intelligence spending resurfaced among prominent investors.
The benchmark S&P 500 index sank 2% during early trading in New York.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 765 points, representing a decline of 1%, retreating from its historic milestone close above 50,000 achieved on Tuesday.
Market confidence was severely shaken by the latest economic data showing that the October Personal Consumption Expenditures price index rose to 4%.
This increase in the preferred inflation measure of the Federal Reserve has heightened anxieties regarding future interest rate decisions right before the Thanksgiving holiday.
Sentiment was further depressed by the announcement of new 20% tariffs by the incoming administration of the United States.
Technology giants led the downward trajectory, with Nvidia, the prominent microchip manufacturer, losing 6% of its market value shortly after trading commenced.
The Cboe Volatility Index, often referred to as the fear gauge of Wall Street, surged above the 30 level to signal heightened anxiety across global financial markets.
8:15 am ET: Wall Street futures fell sharply ahead of the opening bell
US stock futures plunged ahead of the New York opening bell as escalating global tariff threats and a technology sector sell-off dented investor sentiment.
Nasdaq 100 futures shed 3% while S&P 500 futures dropped 2% and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures fell 1% in early trading.
Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD), the artificial intelligence chipmaker, saw its shares slide 5% in premarket trading amid widening concerns over large-scale technology infrastructure spending.
Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT), the recently listed artificial intelligence company, dropped 6% to fall below its initial public offering price.
Workday Inc (NASDAQ:WDAY), the enterprise software provider, fell 10% to $162 despite increasing its financial guidance.
Sentiment across global markets weakened after Jamieson Greer, the US trade representative, signalled the potential implementation of broad import tariffs.
Investors are also trading cautiously ahead of crucial macroeconomic data releases, including the latest personal consumption expenditures inflation gauge and gross domestic product revisions.
1:00 pm GMT: The blue-chip index remains stable while mid-cap companies fall
London's premier equity index stayed flat at one afternoon today as defensive gains balanced wider global market anxieties.
The FTSE 100 index tracking the largest corporations stood at 10464 points.
Investors favored large consumer staples and healthcare companies to cushion against international technology stock declines.
The wider market moves follow renewed pressure on international artificial intelligence shares after significant declines on Wall Street.
Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD), the prominent microprocessor manufacturer, fell 8% to depress global investor sentiment.
Sentiment also remains cautious before the release of personal consumption expenditures inflation data from the United States.
The FTSE 250 index of medium-sized companies experienced heavier selling, sliding 1% to 23696 points.
Mid-cap corporations are typically more exposed to the domestic economy and trade tariff concerns than multinational blue chips.
Domestic consumer confidence has shown only a modest recovery following recent tax updates.
The London Stock Exchange Group PLC (LSE:LSEG) the financial market infrastructure business, saw its own shares advance to 10000p.
The exchange operator recently launched a cash tender offer to buy back outstanding dollar notes.
Traders are also adjusting to higher borrowing costs after the Bank of England raised the benchmark rate to 4%.
The central bank action has kept the British pound volatile against international currencies.
12:00 pm GMT: London's blue-chip index edged higher at midday
London equity markets delivered a fractured performance at midday as a rotation into defensive sectors cushioned large-cap stocks against a broader technology-led retreat.
The FTSE 100 index gained 0.1% to reach 10,482, supported by substantial gains in the healthcare and personal care sectors.
Conversely, the mid-cap FTSE 250 index fell 0.4% to trade at 23,767 as international technology anxieties rippled into domestic mid-market equities.
Market participants heavily favoured defensive household names ahead of crucial inflation readings and prospective tariff announcements from Washington.
Unilever PLC (LSE:ULVR), the consumer goods group, advanced nearly 2% after regulators intimated that a brand disposal could resolve competition concerns tied to a separate food deal.
Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (LSE:RKT, OTCQX:RBGLY), the consumer health manufacturer, also rallied by 2% as asset managers realigned their portfolios into resilient businesses.
Pharmaceutical heavyweight AstraZeneca PLC (LSE:AZN, NYSE:AZN) experienced steady buying interest, with its market valuation strengthening 1% during morning negotiations.
The broader market mood remained constrained by a persistent cooling of the global artificial intelligence expansion, which dampened sentiment across European and Asian trading hubs.
Currency markets saw sterling weaken 0.3% against the US dollar to trade at 1.31, reflecting caution ahead of economic announcements.
Continental markets staged a modest recovery during the session, with the CAC 40 index in Paris adding 0.7% and the DAX index in Frankfurt climbing 0.2%.
11:00 am GMT: Small cap round-up
Cavendish Capital Markets disclosed buying 272,010 and selling 507,756 NextEnergy Solar Fund Ltd (LSE:NESF) shares on 24 November 2026, leaving a 68,026-share holding, equal to 0.01%.
Quantum Helium Ltd (AIM:QHE)'s Sagebrush-1 testing confirmed helium presence but no commercial flow, supporting plans for purpose-built 2027 wells and potential US helium acquisitions.
Sintana Energy Inc (TSX-V:SEI, OTCQB:SEUSF, AIM:SEI) has completed its acquisition of a 5% indirect interest in Angola's KON-16 block, ahead of planned 2027 exploration drilling.
genedrive PLC (AIM:GDR) has raised up to £1.23 million through a 1.3p-per-share subscription, a 72.4% premium, to fund working capital and accelerate commercial adoption of its diagnostic tests.
Strategic Minerals PLC (AIM:SML)' Redmoor tungsten project has secured a £2m non-dilutive KIGF grant to accelerate infill drilling and integrated PFS-to-DFS feasibility work through March 2029.
Empyrean Energy PLC (AIM:EME) expects to mobilise a rig on 4 January 2027 to drill the 8.3 BCF GOLD-1 gas prospect in Austria, with estimated investment of €3.7 million and potential net revenue of €34.8 million.
Bradda Head Lithium Ltd (AIM:BHL) reported its strongest Whistlejacket drill result to date, intersecting 38.13m at 1.34% Li₂O, including 23.39m at 1.62%, while noting slower-than-planned drilling progress.
10.00 am GMT: Burberry tops FTSE 100 risers
Burberry led the FTSE 100 market leaders on Wednesday, climbing 3.62% to 1,203p as consumer stocks attracted buyers amid a global technology sell-off.
The FTSE 100 advanced 38.31 points, or 0.37%, to 10,505.38, easing from stronger gains earlier in the session.
Tobacco giant Imperial Brands gained 2.28% to 2,921p, while investment group 3i advanced 2.23% to 2,709p.
B&Q owner Kingfisher rose 2% to 378.4p, supported by buying across consumer-facing stocks.
Household goods groups Reckitt Benckiser and Unilever also featured among the market leaders, gaining 1.89% to 5,816p and 1.68% to 5,039p respectively.
The gains reflected investor interest in established consumer businesses as technology shares remained under pressure globally ahead of US inflation figures due at 1.30pm GMT.
9.00 am GMT: Defensive stocks dominate
The FTSE 100 gained 58points, or 0.55%, to 10,524.81, while the FTSE 250 rose 0.16% to 23,896.92.
Burberry led FTSE 100 risers on Wednesday, climbing 2.88% to 1,194.5p as investors favoured consumer-facing companies amid a global technology sell-off.
B&Q owner Kingfisher advanced 2.32% to 379.6p, while investment group 3i rose 1.96% to 2,702p.
Housebuilder Barratt Redrow gained 1.95% to 308.6p, with Premier Inn owner Whitbread adding 1.87% and aerospace manufacturer Melrose Industries rising 1.81%.
Technology-related stocks remained under pressure, with Auto Trader falling 2.07%, Computacenter losing 1.27% and Sage declining 1.27%.
Among mid-cap stocks, Pets at Home surged 8.81% to 284.2p following stronger first-half results, while Wizz Air climbed 3.15% and International Workplace Group gained 2.75%.
Funding Circle led FTSE 250 fallers, dropping 6.15%, followed by Auction Technology Group, down 4.52%, and Ocado, which lost 4.43%.
The contrasting performances highlighted continued investor demand for consumer and defensive shares as concerns over artificial intelligence valuations weighed on technology stocks.
8.30 am GMT: FTSE 100 rallies as consumer stocks lead gains
The FTSE 100 rose 68.65 points, or 0.66%, to 10,535.72 in early trading on Wednesday, as consumer and retail stocks rallied despite overnight weakness in US and Asian technology shares.
Compass Group, Unilever and Kingfisher led the blue-chip advance, each gaining around 2%, while JD Sports and Coca-Cola HBC also moved higher.
Pets at Home surged 9.71% after the pet retailer reported a 44.2% rise in first-half pre-tax profit to £52.2 million and raised its full-year expectations to the top end of analyst forecasts.
Budget airline easyJet edged 0.09% higher despite reporting an 89% fall in annual headline pre-tax profit to £71 million, as higher fuel costs and weaker demand weighed on earnings.
European markets also advanced, with Germany's DAX and France's CAC 40 trading higher.
Investors are awaiting US personal consumption expenditures inflation data at 1.30pm GMT, followed by remarks from Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey and fellow policymakers.
Brent crude fell 1.8% to US$87.16 a barrel, while gold also weakened.
7.00 am GMT: FTSE 100 faces pressure as AI sell-off spreads
The FTSE 100 is expected to open cautiously on Wednesday, with December futures last quoted at 10,518, down 9.9 points, or 0.09%, in early trading.
London's blue-chip index closed Tuesday down 13.75 points, or 0.13%, at 10,467.07, while the FTSE 250 lost 0.84%.
Wall Street ended mixed overnight, with the Nasdaq falling 1.48% and the S&P 500 losing 0.5%, although the Dow gained 0.85%.
Nvidia dropped 5.9%, reigniting concerns over artificial intelligence valuations.
Asian markets followed lower, with Taiwan's Taiex tumbling more than 6%, South Korea's Kospi sliding around 5.6% and Japan's Nikkei losing more than 3%.
The S&P/ASX 200 fell 34 points, or 0.39%, to close at 8,692.40 on Wednesday, as annual inflation surged to 4.9%, raising concerns over further interest rate hikes by the Reserve Bank of Australia.
Bitcoin has fallen below US$60,000 as renewed selling across cryptocurrency markets wipes out a short-lived recovery, with institutional investors withdrawing almost US$4.7 billion from US Bitcoin exchange-traded funds in November.
Investors will watch US inflation data later today, alongside Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey's appearance before MPs.

Tobacco giant Imperial Brands gained 2.28% to 2,921p, while investment group 3i advanced 2.23% to 2,709p.
B&Q owner Kingfisher rose 2% to 378.4p, supported by buying across consumer-facing stocks.
Household goods groups Reckitt Benckiser and Unilever also featured among the market leaders, gaining 1.89% to 5,816p and 1.68% to 5,039p respectively.
The gains reflected investor interest in established consumer businesses as technology shares remained under pressure globally ahead of US inflation figures due at 1.30pm GMT.
9.00 am GMT: Defensive stocks dominate
The FTSE 100 gained 58points, or 0.55%, to 10,524.81, while the FTSE 250 rose 0.16% to 23,896.92.
Burberry led FTSE 100 risers on Wednesday, climbing 2.88% to 1,194.5p as investors favoured consumer-facing companies amid a global technology sell-off.
B&Q owner Kingfisher advanced 2.32% to 379.6p, while investment group 3i rose 1.96% to 2,702p.
Housebuilder Barratt Redrow gained 1.95% to 308.6p, with Premier Inn owner Whitbread adding 1.87% and aerospace manufacturer Melrose Industries rising 1.81%.
Technology-related stocks remained under pressure, with Auto Trader falling 2.07%, Computacenter losing 1.27% and Sage declining 1.27%.
Among mid-cap stocks, Pets at Home surged 8.81% to 284.2p following stronger first-half results, while Wizz Air climbed 3.15% and International Workplace Group gained 2.75%.
Funding Circle led FTSE 250 fallers, dropping 6.15%, followed by Auction Technology Group, down 4.52%, and Ocado, which lost 4.43%.
The contrasting performances highlighted continued investor demand for consumer and defensive shares as concerns over artificial intelligence valuations weighed on technology stocks.
8.30 am GMT: FTSE 100 rallies as consumer stocks lead gains
The FTSE 100 rose 68.65 points, or 0.66%, to 10,535.72 in early trading on Wednesday, as consumer and retail stocks rallied despite overnight weakness in US and Asian technology shares.
Compass Group, Unilever and Kingfisher led the blue-chip advance, each gaining around 2%, while JD Sports and Coca-Cola HBC also moved higher.
Pets at Home surged 9.71% after the pet retailer reported a 44.2% rise in first-half pre-tax profit to £52.2 million and raised its full-year expectations to the top end of analyst forecasts.
Budget airline easyJet edged 0.09% higher despite reporting an 89% fall in annual headline pre-tax profit to £71 million, as higher fuel costs and weaker demand weighed on earnings.
European markets also advanced, with Germany's DAX and France's CAC 40 trading higher.
Investors are awaiting US personal consumption expenditures inflation data at 1.30pm GMT, followed by remarks from Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey and fellow policymakers.
Brent crude fell 1.8% to US$87.16 a barrel, while gold also weakened.
7.00 am GMT: FTSE 100 faces pressure as AI sell-off spreads
The FTSE 100 is expected to open cautiously on Wednesday, with December futures last quoted at 10,518, down 9.9 points, or 0.09%, in early trading.
London's blue-chip index closed Tuesday down 13.75 points, or 0.13%, at 10,467.07, while the FTSE 250 lost 0.84%.
Wall Street ended mixed overnight, with the Nasdaq falling 1.48% and the S&P 500 losing 0.5%, although the Dow gained 0.85%.
Nvidia dropped 5.9%, reigniting concerns over artificial intelligence valuations.
Asian markets followed lower, with Taiwan's Taiex tumbling more than 6%, South Korea's Kospi sliding around 5.6% and Japan's Nikkei losing more than 3%.
The S&P/ASX 200 fell 34 points, or 0.39%, to close at 8,692.40 on Wednesday, as annual inflation surged to 4.9%, raising concerns over further interest rate hikes by the Reserve Bank of Australia.

Bitcoin has fallen below US$60,000 as renewed selling across cryptocurrency markets wipes out a short-lived recovery, with institutional investors withdrawing almost US$4.7 billion from US Bitcoin exchange-traded funds in November.
Investors will watch US inflation data later today, alongside Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey's appearance before MPs.
